To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the best method of benthic cover assessment for coral reef habitats was found to be the digital photographic analysis of a 5 x 5 m grid with a 1024 point sampling.
the photographic transects using 1024-point analysis is the overall best choice of method, provided there are no limits on the resources and expertise available.

the 1024 point method of digital photographic analysis is the most effective and efficient method for mapping coral reefs from remotely sensed data; the method is also suitable for validating image based maps; the method is applicable to any remotely sensed image with lower spectral or radiometric resolution; the method is suitable for any image with lower spatial resolution, provided that the spatial resolution is greater than 5m; and that the method can be applied by scientists or managers with no special expertise
In summary, our research is concerned with
the integration of remote sensing and field data in the mapping of coral reef habitats.
developing a method of field survey and analysis of digital images to validate maps derived from remotely-sensed images of coral reefs.
developing a methodology for the validation of coral reef habitat maps derived from remotely-sensed data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best technique for mapping benthic cover is to use a digital photographic transect with 1024 point digital analysis, but this technique is not suitable for all situations.

(a) the photographic transect with 1024 point image analysis is the best technique for validating maps derived from remote sensing, and (b) the photographic transects with five point analysis and the photographic quadrats with 1024 points are also suitable techniques.
the photographic transects using 1024 points is the best choice for field validation of remotely sensed imagery.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a 5.5 x 5.5 m photographic transect with 1024 points is an excellent method for field validation of remotely sensed data, but the method is time and labour intensive.
a combination of the point intercept transect method, with 1024 point digital image analysis is the most efficient method for field validation of maps derived remotely sensed data.
a photographic transect using a 1024 point digital analysis is the best technique for field validation of coral reef habitat mapping derived from remotely sensed image data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the photographic transects using 1024 points are the best method for mapping coral reefs, and the best method to verify image-based maps.
the photographic transects using 1024 points is a good method for validating maps derived from airborne imagery.
the photographic transects using 1024-point processing are a good choice for field validation of maps derived remotely sensed images.
